page.layout: One page of text: a Latin poem in verse, set as 7 stanzas of four lines each, indented in a staggered pattern. Catchword at the lower right, below the last line. No margin notes.

main_text.p: Hic dum sagaces prouidus explicat Curas,amicis dum timet anxius Hostisque dum fraudes recludit, Quæ mala,quoue tulit labores !
Nullæ rigenti frigore territum Videre Brumæ aut Andromedes Pater, Et stella vesani Leonis, Cum segetes coquit æstus almas.
Tantisque tandem mortibus addite, Condæ Princeps,quo tua carmine Dicenda,quo sletu riganda Fata truci properata fraude?
Non præliantem perdidit hostilicus Ensis duello,classica cum sonant, Armata quando militantes Per medias rapit ira cædes.
Sed tu occidisti,progenies bona Magni parentis,Borbonicæ altera Spes gentis occultis venenis Insidiis superatus atri,
Quo delibutis muneribus ferox Medea quondam Colchica pellicem Est vlta,quo parens superbis Sæviit imperiis Locusta.
Has prisca fraudes Gallia nesciens Virtute sola & Marte potentior Latè per obstantes caternas Explicuit sua signa victrix

page.notes: Two ornamental signs before "Andromedes" (line 6) and "Marte" (line 26) appear to be astronomical or planetary symbols; I could not read them with certainty, so I did not transcribe them. The stanza breaks follow the indentation pattern; the verse reads as continuous. Spelling u/v is normalised (e.g. "prouidus" to "providus" in print, but kept as "Vlta" with capital U as printed: "Est vlta" transcribed as "Est vlta"). Show-through from the facing page is ignored.
